description.narrative: After the fall of the Saleh regime in 2011, the country has been drawn into a conflict with national, regional and international actors. The country is facing a tremendous humanitarian crisis. Civic space is very limited, since organisations face a lack of protection, funding, capacity and support. Against this backdrop, the SCC programme in Yemen is crucial to create a safe space for CSOs to act and to play active role towards ending the conflict.

The activity is part of a larger programme implemented by the Strengthening Civil Courage Alliance, consisting of ABAAD – Resource Center for Gender Equality, Amnesty International The Netherlands, DefendDefenders, PAX and their partner networks.

The main objective of the SCC programme in Yemen is for Yemeni civilians represented by civil society play an active role towards building inclusive peace, reducing civilian suffering through arms control and environmental protection, and ensuring accountability at the local, national and international level. The aim is to expand civic space, particularly by women and youth-led civil society, for civil society to gain access to accountability processes, and strengthen international standards and due diligence on arms control.
The target groups are local partner organisations; activists; local councils; small CSOs; national actors; and the international community. A particular focus is on women and youth.

title.narrative: # of CSOs with increased L&A capacities (women-led)

comment.narrative: In Yemen, 2 partners (1 women and youth -led, 1 women-led) analysed their L & A capacities in 8 capacity areas (A.Produce evidence, B. inspire trust among power holders, C represent constituency interests, D. Analyse the political arena, E. Produce tailored messages, F work collectibely, G. Build rapport with power hjolders, H. Adpat to ongoing environmental changes )-, determining the need to prioritize strengthening the capacity to analyze the political arena.

In October 2023, a session on advocacy will be organized during the Yemen partner meeting. All partners will attend. The content will be defined based on the L&A assessment that was conducted in 2022, discussed with the partners beforehand, and probably focused on the ability to conduct stakeholder and institutional analysis. As a next step, an online (assessment refreshing) session will be organized in Q1-2024 by PAX with Resonate and the CAP to identify further advocacy capacity needs and ways of addressing them. Both CAP and Resonate were considered in preious L&A activities in 2022 and 2023 so won't be counted for the quantitative target of 2024.

By the end of 2024, the partners strengthened their L&A capacities in areas D. Analyse the political arena (Jan: gender-sensitive conflict analysis and detailed problem analysis during partner meeting), E. Produce tailored messages + F work collectively + G. Build rapport with power holders (Jan: during advocacy workshop and March/April: in preparation of advocacy meetings in Brussels and The Hague). Delayed start of L&A activities due to rejected/delayed visas combined with ensuing difficulties to meet in the region after 7 October 2023. Evidently, partners strengthened their skills in area H. Adapt to ongoing environmental changes and reflected this in their L&A efforts.

By the end of 2022, 1 partner organisation (Women-led) will have strengthened their lobby & advocacy (L&A) capacities in capacity area D. This area covers the following organizational requirements: Ability to conduct stakeholder and institutional analysis; access to information; knowledge of relevant laws, policies and treaties.

In 2022, CSOs have strenghtened their capacities in capacity area D, the capacity to analyse the political arena. One online digital security training was organized by PAX for one women-led CSO and for one women and youth-led CSO to enhance knowlegde on the safe access and handeling of information requirement.

In 2022, a lobby & advocacy (L&A) capacity assessmnet was conducted in 2022 twoa partners, one women led, the other both women and youth led. The assesssmnet showed a need to work on capacity area D of analysing the political arena. This area covers the following organizational requirements: Ability to conduct stakeholder and institutional analysis; access to information; knowledge of relevant laws, policies and treaties. In 2022, one online digital security training was organized by PAX to enhance knowlegde on the safe access and handeling of information requirement. The focus in 2023 will be on the ability to conduct stakeholder and institutional analysis.
2025 annual target: A series of online sessions for building organizations' advocacy strategy will be organized by PAX for Resonate, CAP & Mwatana.

title.narrative: Outcome 3.2 The Dutch government has strengthened its arms export policy and has led international discussions on restricting arms exports to Yemen.
# of policies adopted by the Dutch government for restricting further its weapons exports to Yemen as a result of the engagement of PoV CSOs (SCS2)

comment.narrative: NL has leading role internationally with a strict export policy regarding Yemen, but a few loopholes remain that should be tackled
NL government leads by example by applying presumption of denial for exports to all Saudi/UAE-led coalition partners.

2022: Nothing really happened in this area, as Yemen largely moved to the background - in part due to the war in Ukraine, and also due to the Yemen ceasefire much, in itself of course a good development 2023: Dutch government has weakened its arms export policy by stopping its presumption of denial policy. PAX has strongly argued against this change, both in the media, in the Parliament as well as in talks with the ministry. 2024: In contrast the Dutch have just relaxed standards for export to S-Arabia and the UAE

title.narrative: Outcome 2.1 Local organizations conduct joint advocacy targeted at Yemeni justice and prosecutorial institutions and UN bodies to advocate for justice and accountability for victims and survivors of human rights violations, including those against women and youth.
# of advocacy initiatives (incl. briefs & reports) carried out by PoV partner CSOs for their victims and survivors of HR violations (SCS4)

comment.narrative: No advocacy inititaives have started yet within this programme. Under this outcome, training will be conducted with field researchers, lawyers and other CSOs which will improve the quality of reporting and produce evidence-based reports. This in turn support advocacy campaigns and initiatives in the coming years of this programme.
At least 4 high impact briefs/reports produced which aim to advocate for justice and accountability for victims and survivors of human rights violations

2022: No advocacy activities have taken place yet. The focus in 2022 was mainly on building the partner's training capacity and the development of 3 manuals, including on MDR; scientific human rights research; and on the provision of legal support to the victims of arbitrary detention, enforced disappearance, and torture 2023: No advocacy activities have taken place in 2023, The focus was mainly on building the partner's capacity. Advocacy activities are planned in 2024 2024: No advocacy activities have taken place in 2024 as a result of the decision to pause the MDR field work due to the security situation. The advocacy Blogs/statements were supposed to be produced by Mwatana and other CSOs based on the documentation of Human rights violation Cases. In 2025 the work was planned be more focusing on Advocacy, but as the collaboration was terminated this will not be achieved.

title.narrative: # of CSOs included in SPs (Strategic Partners) programmes (women-led)

comment.narrative: These partner organizations are valued by other international NGOs and have good connections with the Dutch Embassy in Yemen. They are well-perceived locally. Their work shows strong commitment towards peace in Yemen and is focused on advocay work, which is essential in this programme.

The partnership with these organizations started in the second half of 2021 and PAX is working on strengthening the connections with each partner organization and between all partners. Creating a strong coordination base will contribute to collectively achieving the objectives of this programme.

3; PAX has a written agreement with 3 partner organizations. Amnesty international has a written agreement with one partner organisation as well with a focus on increasing capacities on monitoring and documenting human rights violations. The ambition is to continue working with these three organizations for the rest of the programme period. New partners might be identified in case of an adding-value opportunity is identified and financial space is available.
A strong coordination and communication base has been established among all partners working on this programme.

The partnership agreement with three CSOs (two women-led, one women and youth-led) continued in 2022 and the coordination between all partners has been strengthened. Understanding of each other's work has improved, hence the ability to identify cross-cutting work and supporting one another increased.

The partnership agreement with the three partner organizations will continue in 2023. Wherever possible, linkages are created between the work of local partners, e.g., exchanges during planning and implemantation are ensured including of experiences and knowladge. This creates stronger connections between Yemeni CSOs.

The partnership agreement with the three partner organizations will continue in 2024. Wherever possible, linkages are created between the work of local partners, e.g., exchanges during planning and implemantation are ensured including of experiences and knowladge. This creates stronger connections between Yemeni CSOs.

The partnership agreement with the three partner organizations will continue in 2025. Wherever possible, linkages are created between the work of local partners, e.g., exchanges during planning and implemantation are ensured including of experiences and knowladge. This creates stronger connections between Yemeni CSOs.
